name: Manufacturing and industrial
description: Production, supply chain, and industrial B2B.

hasDefinedTerm.name: OEM
hasDefinedTerm.description: Original equipment manufacturer. The company that produced a part or system under its own name.

hasDefinedTerm.name: ODM
hasDefinedTerm.description: Original design manufacturer. A supplier that designs as well as builds, for another brand to sell.

hasDefinedTerm.name: contract manufacturing
hasDefinedTerm.description: Outsourced production to a supplier's specification and capacity.

hasDefinedTerm.name: BOM
hasDefinedTerm.description: The structured list of every component required to build a product.

hasDefinedTerm.name: MOQ
hasDefinedTerm.description: Minimum order quantity. The smallest batch a supplier will produce.

hasDefinedTerm.name: manufacturing lead time
hasDefinedTerm.description: Elapsed time from placing an order to receiving it.

hasDefinedTerm.name: takt time
hasDefinedTerm.description: The production pace required to meet customer demand.

hasDefinedTerm.name: cycle time
hasDefinedTerm.description: How long one unit takes to move through a process.

hasDefinedTerm.name: throughput
hasDefinedTerm.description: Units produced per unit of time.

hasDefinedTerm.name: OEE
hasDefinedTerm.description: Overall equipment effectiveness. Availability times performance times quality.

hasDefinedTerm.name: process yield
hasDefinedTerm.description: The share of units produced that meet specification.

hasDefinedTerm.name: scrap rate
hasDefinedTerm.description: The share of material lost to defects or waste.

hasDefinedTerm.name: rework
hasDefinedTerm.description: Correcting defective output rather than scrapping it.

hasDefinedTerm.name: tolerance
hasDefinedTerm.description: The permitted deviation from a specified dimension.

hasDefinedTerm.name: GD&T
hasDefinedTerm.description: Geometric dimensioning and tolerancing. A standard notation for specifying allowable variation.

hasDefinedTerm.name: CNC
hasDefinedTerm.description: Computer numerical control. Machining driven by programmed instructions.

hasDefinedTerm.name: CAD
hasDefinedTerm.description: Computer-aided design. Software for producing engineering drawings and models.

hasDefinedTerm.name: CAM
hasDefinedTerm.description: Computer-aided manufacturing. Software translating designs into machine instructions.

hasDefinedTerm.name: additive manufacturing
hasDefinedTerm.description: Building parts by adding material layer by layer rather than cutting it away.

hasDefinedTerm.name: injection moulding
hasDefinedTerm.description: Forming parts by forcing molten material into a tool. High tooling cost, low unit cost at volume.

hasDefinedTerm.name: tooling
hasDefinedTerm.description: The dies, moulds, and fixtures required to produce a part.

hasDefinedTerm.name: prototype
hasDefinedTerm.description: An early build used to validate design before committing to production tooling.

hasDefinedTerm.name: new product introduction
hasDefinedTerm.description: Taking a design from validated prototype into stable production. Distinct from the healthcare NPI, which is a provider identifier.

hasDefinedTerm.name: lean manufacturing
hasDefinedTerm.description: A method focused on removing activity that does not add customer value.

hasDefinedTerm.name: Six Sigma
hasDefinedTerm.description: A method for reducing process variation using statistical analysis.

hasDefinedTerm.name: kaizen
hasDefinedTerm.description: Continuous incremental improvement driven by the people doing the work.

hasDefinedTerm.name: kanban
hasDefinedTerm.description: A pull-based signalling system that triggers replenishment only when stock is consumed.

hasDefinedTerm.name: just in time
hasDefinedTerm.description: Receiving material only as production needs it. Efficient, and fragile under supply shock.

hasDefinedTerm.name: MRP
hasDefinedTerm.description: Material requirements planning. Scheduling purchases and production from a demand forecast.

hasDefinedTerm.name: ERP
hasDefinedTerm.description: Enterprise resource planning. The system of record spanning finance, inventory, and production.

hasDefinedTerm.name: MES
hasDefinedTerm.description: Manufacturing execution system. Software tracking and controlling work on the shop floor.

hasDefinedTerm.name: SCADA
hasDefinedTerm.description: Supervisory control and data acquisition. Systems monitoring and controlling industrial equipment.

hasDefinedTerm.name: PLC
hasDefinedTerm.description: Programmable logic controller. The industrial computer running machine control logic.

hasDefinedTerm.name: predictive maintenance
hasDefinedTerm.description: Using condition data to service equipment before it fails.

hasDefinedTerm.name: ISO 9001
hasDefinedTerm.description: The international standard for quality management systems.

hasDefinedTerm.name: traceability
hasDefinedTerm.description: The ability to follow a part's history through materials, process, and handling.

hasDefinedTerm.name: supply chain resilience
hasDefinedTerm.description: The capacity to keep producing when a supplier, route, or input fails.

hasDefinedTerm.name: nearshoring
hasDefinedTerm.description: Relocating production closer to the end market to shorten and de-risk supply.

hasDefinedTerm.name: spec sheet
hasDefinedTerm.description: The document stating a product's dimensions, materials, and performance. High-intent content in industrial search.

hasDefinedTerm.name: RFQ
hasDefinedTerm.description: Request for quote. A buyer's formal request for pricing against a specification.
